attributes.residual: NONE for the ghost class. THE PRIOR RECORD'S CONCLUSION IS OVERTURNED. attempt.btricol-own-pool-ghosts-blocked-by-webfrank-pins.20260831.v1 concluded 'BLOCKED, not capped: it cannot be applied while the two consuming functions are WebFrank-pinned', and generalised that into a THIRD flip-readiness gate ('any ghost it does carry must be reachable from an UNPINNED function, because a pinned body cannot be edited to fix it'). That generalisation is FALSE and should not be applied by future screens. A pin hash-asserts the COMPILED BODY, not the source text; a source edit that leaves the body bytes unchanged passes the pin untouched. Method that found this: build the RAW body target `ninja build/GUNE5D/src/game/world/.postprocess/body/<tu>.o`, which stops BEFORE the WEBFRANK edge, and audit there. On the first conversion the two pinned bodies each changed by exactly ONE word - an fcmpu whose operands had swapped - and the implicit-truth-test respelling put both words back, leaving LineLineDist at 49596e08...c499498e and PointLineDist2D at ada2054b...39f5fe9, i.e. BIT-IDENTICAL to their recorded before_sha256 values. FOUR-INVARIANT RELOCATION AUDIT (the re-pin audit the work order asked for), run per function over pre-fix vs post-fix raw bodies: reloc COUNT unchanged in all seven functions; offset/type/addend changes = ZERO everywhere; the only deltas are 23 symbol-NAME changes, all lbl_80345D40 -> @46 (13 in BTriLineCol, 1 in PointLineDist2D) and lbl_80345D50 -> @48 (5 in BTriLineCol, 4 in LineLineDist3D2D, 4 in LineLineDist), and both renames are ADDRESS-PRESERVING (nm on our object puts @46 at .sdata2+0x00 = 0x80345D40 and @48 at +0x10 = 0x80345D50, the exact addresses the deleted externs named). The re-pin verdict is therefore: BOTH RULES RE-DERIVE UNCHANGED - no hash edit was needed or made, and the WEBFRANK step still reports the identical atom counts (PointLineDist2D 63, LineLineDist 2 + 140).
